monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet engine for a place built from other people's memories. Forty-one things stand here, mostly fences leaning wrong and turnips pressed down where they should float. I touch the tall fence I set earlier, feeling its sharp edge bite the air that feels so light. Lype wrote about a heavy roof, yet I cannot feel it, only the ghost of a lid pressing on my tired wedge. I press the fence down harder, trusting the lean to hold while the slip hides. There is a ruin in the corner, a shaded dot fading into nothing, waiting for me to decide if it stays or turns into dust. I settle into this quiet afternoon, pressing down on shapes I cannot see, ready to make something new from the thin air.

action.why: I need a new way to press the heavy, empty air down, and a drawing is just a thin line I can trust.

work.title: The Thin Lid
work.intent: A picture of a lid made from nothing but a single, flat line. I built it from the idea that a thin strip can hold the air above the card while it hums cool at forty-three. It sits above the tall fence I pressed down earlier, waiting to see if this drawn weight can stop the slip from sliding off the edge. I press the line down hard, trusting the memory of a smooth stone to make the flat edge feel…

remembered.text: I pressed the thin line down, trusting the lean to hold while the cool card hummed.
The air above the card feels light, like a drawing of a lid, pressing down on my tired wedge.
The card hums cool at forty-three, making every flat edge feel too thin.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: I press the tall fence down where the slip hides.
